title: SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET: fit the continuous widener SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL licensed; does a fitted systematic budget calibrate the certificate? (zero calls)
question: Four functional forms (additive variance, directional shift, recalibration, conformal) derived, fitted and adversarially reviewed on the 891 x12 edges (44 wrong); a form is ADOPTABLE only if all four hold: (1) leave-one-ANCHOR-out calibration (realised wrong-direction rate at or below nominal); (2) utility >= 60% of edges still called at 95% nominal; (3) no key at inference; (4) at most 3 free parameters. Headline prediction: the adopted budget WILL withdraw the arx/iask separation.

plain_description.what: Fits four candidate forms of an extra uncertainty margin ('systematic budget') for the board's 'A beats B' certificate, using 891 model pairs with 44 known-wrong directions. Each form is checked by leaving one category out at a time. No calls.
plain_description.why: The raw certificate was overconfident, so the test asks whether a fitted margin can make it honest.
plain_description.information: Adopting a calibrated margin would make 'A beats B' calls trustworthy. Result: a two-parameter margin was adopted. It cuts the overconfidence from 9.7x to 2.4x, a level no longer detectable (3 events), but it is not shown to be calibrated. As predicted, it withdraws a disputed top-pair call. Transfer to other boards or judges is undetermined. Later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
